text:
maria: FYI — support found a customer payload that fails on POST /v1/files/upload. Docs show "metadata" as an object, but our S3 integration expects an array of key/value pairs. Customer got a 400.
aj: Can you paste the failing request?
maria: From support: `curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/files/upload" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"file_url":"https://...","metadata":{"owner":"alice","env":"prod"}}'` -> 400 {"error":"invalid metadata format"}
kevin: Root cause: OpenAPI schema currently models metadata as an object (additionalProperties), runtime expects `array` of `{key,value}`. I'll open a docs PR to change the schema and add matching examples.
docs-bot: kevin opened PR #2345: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2345
samir: Before merging, call out backwards compatibility and SDK impact. Python and JS clients will keep sending dicts by default; Go too. We need a migration snippet for each SDK and a deprecation note.
aj: Could server accept both shapes temporarily?
maria: Ops can support both shapes for API versions <= v1.2 for ~90 days, but will remove the object form afterwards. Docs must show transformation and mention duplicate-key and ordering behavior.
kevin: Draft PR includes small examples and transforms:
- curl example showing array form: `{"metadata":[{"key":"owner","value":"alice"}]}`
- python helper: `if isinstance(metadata, dict): metadata = [{"key":k, "value":v} for k,v in metadata.items()]`
- js helper snippet using `Object.entries(metadata).map(([k,v])=>({key:k,value:v}))`
- go helper: `func Convert(m map[string]string) []Metadata { ... }`
aj: Add explicit note: object form will lose duplicate keys and insertion order depends on language; array preserves duplicates and order.
samir: Also add a docs CI check that validates the included examples against the OpenAPI schema (so example payloads are linted). I'll add a small json-schema test in the docs repo.
maria: I'll draft the support KB and changelog blurb and coordinate the notice. Once CI is green, we can merge and schedule the prod docs deploy. Thanks! :tada:
